prompt: An organization is enabling Claude Code for several teams. It needs to prevent unapproved model use and detect spend spikes before they affect the monthly budget. What should administrators establish before broad access?

options.text: Ask users to choose whichever model they prefer and review total spend after month end.
Define approved model availability/defaults and effort guidance, set appropriate spend/rate limits and per-user visibility, and monitor alerts before widening the rollout.
Use a single low-cost model for every task and disable usage reporting to avoid sensitive data collection.
Let teams share credentials so usage appears as one predictable account.

feedback.reason: Model choice and spend are operational guardrails; set ownership and visibility before broad enablement rather than relying on post-month review.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The supported controls vary by product and organization setup; verify exact model, limit, and reporting capabilities before claiming enforcement.
details.scenarioApplication: Model choice and spend are operational guardrails; set ownership and visibility before broad enablement rather than relying on post-month review.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Usage visibility should avoid collecting unnecessary prompt content; the requirement here is spend telemetry and limits.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternatives change a different layer, leave the stated risk uncontrolled, or claim more evidence than the scenario supplies.
details.transfer: Choose controls tied to budget and approved-use policy, then verify their effective operation.

prompt: A company’s fixed monthly cap is shared by five departments with very different expected request volume. A single global alert fires only after 95% of the cap is used. What should the rollout owner add?

options.text: Remove the cap because local teams understand their usage better.
Set all five departments to the same low hard limit regardless of their work.
Allocate owner-reviewed budgets or thresholds by expected usage, add earlier warning and per-user/department visibility, and retain a defined response when limits are reached.
Wait for an overage and then infer which department used the most from the final invoice.

feedback.reason: A late global alert lacks actionable ownership and may conceal one team’s spike; budget guardrails should match the organization’s usage model.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Cost attribution and limits need to be aligned with who owns budget decisions and how the system behaves at the limit.
details.scenarioApplication: A late global alert lacks actionable ownership and may conceal one team’s spike; budget guardrails should match the organization’s usage model.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A strict per-team cap can disrupt legitimate work; define escalation and exception processes.
details.errorCorrection: The tempting alternatives change a different layer, leave the stated risk uncontrolled, or claim more evidence than the scenario supplies.
details.transfer: Make spend posture observable and actionable before rollout.

prompt: A team’s spend rises sharply after enabling an agent workflow that can make several calls per request. What should the admin compare before raising the team limit?

options.text: Only the advertised per-token price of the selected model.
The number of enabled users, assuming each request causes one call.
The monthly bill against the previous month without analyzing workload changes.
Expected and actual requests, calls per request, input/output tokens, retries, routing, and outcomes by workflow; then adjust the budget or architecture with an owner.

feedback.reason: Agentic interaction shape can multiply call and token usage, so a simple user count or unit price misses the drivers.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Spend growth may be acceptable if it buys valuable outcomes; compare cost against the workload and quality achieved.

prompt: A model has a provider-level monthly spend limit but no project budget, team owner, or alert recipient. What is the main gap before the organization-wide rollout?

options.text: The limit lacks an operating owner and actionable notification path; assign budget responsibility, alert recipients, and a response policy, with more granular limits if needed.
The provider must lower its token price before any team can use the model.
The team should store a shared API key so all spend aggregates in one place.
A system prompt should instruct users to limit expensive tasks.

feedback.reason: A ceiling without ownership and response does not tell the organization who acts when the budget is near its limit.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Spend controls include who owns thresholds, who receives signals, and what the team does when they trigger.
details.scenarioApplication: A ceiling without ownership and response does not tell the organization who acts when the budget is near its limit.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Granularity depends on the organization’s product/account features; do not assume per-user controls unless verified.

details.transfer: Make guardrails actionable and proportionate to actual usage ownership.
